newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ASM Litho year results seen higher.
newsitem.headline: ASM Litho year results seen higher.

text.p: The 1996 net profit of Dutch semiconductor equipment maker ASM Lithography NV is expected to show a strong improvement, boosted by higher sales and margin improvements, analysts said on Friday.

ASML, in which Philips Electronics NV holds a 35 percent stake, is expected to announce net earnings next Thursday of between 210 million and 241 million guilders, up from the 131.4 million net reported for calendar 1995.
"ASML has improved its sales and its product mix, gained market share and increased profitability via higher margins," said ING Barings analyst Eric de Graaf.
De Graaf is forecasting a 1996 net profit of 210.8 million guilders, while his earnings per share target is 6.15 guilders against the 4.06 guilders reported by ASML for 1995.
He said the delivery of ASML's "wafer steppers" ordered before the second half should help the sales number and boost the bottom line, as should the sale of more advanced models.

Wafer steppers are highly sensitive machines using complex photolithography techniques to make semiconductors and integrated circuits. ASML said in July it shipped 98 machines during the first half of 1996. Analysts reckon it shipped 100-105 in the second half bringing a 1996 total of over 200.
ASML sold 177 steppers in 1995, generating 918 million guilders of sales during the year.

Gert Jochems of NIB Strating is at the upper end of forecasts with his 241.5 million guilder net profit prediction. "ASML had a very good first half with a lot of deliveries," he said, adding his forecast was based on "clearly higher sales."
He said ASML looked like it had been gaining market share from its main competitors, while De Graaf said general cost cutting had helped improve margins.
De Graaf said he was looking for operating margins of 25 percent for 1996, up from around 23 percent the previous year.
Analysts said they would be looking closely at the results for any further clues on order books and trading prospects.
The company said in July it saw uncertainty over its growth prospects in 1997 as the business climate changed.
It said then that it saw growth picking up in 1998 in line with semi-conductor market growth expectations. -- Keiron Henderson, Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5000
